description: A professional dermatologist-inspired skincare routine designed to address melasma concerns, focusing on daily and nightly routines with additional weekly treatments.
estimated_time: 30 minutes per day, including a maximum of 15 minutes for the weekly treatment session.

morning_steps.purpose: Protects skin from UV rays which can worsen melasma
Promotes collagen production and helps lighten hyperpigmentation

morning_steps.action: Apply a peptide cream or gel
morning_steps.purpose: Improves skin texture and reduces the appearance of melasma patches

night_steps.purpose: Removes impurities and prepares skin for nighttime treatments

night_steps.action: Use a retinol cream or serum
night_steps.purpose: Stimulates cell turnover, enhances skin repair, and helps prevent new melasma spots

night_steps.action: Apply a broad-spectrum sunscreen SPF 30 or higher
night_steps.purpose: Protects skin from UV rays during the day even when not directly exposed to sunlight

weekly_steps.action: Apply a chemical peel or use a retinoid treatment mask

dont: Avoid excessive sun exposure without proper protection
Do not pick or scratch the skin, as this can worsen melasma and cause scarring
common_mistakes: Failing to protect the skin from UV rays
Using products that may irritate the skin
best_products_categories: Chemical Peels and Retinoid Treatment Masks

expected_results.2_weeks: Skin appears brighter, fine lines may be less visible, and new melasma spots are reduced
expected_results.1_month: Visible improvement in skin tone and texture with a reduction in the appearance of old melasma spots
expected_results.3_months: Significant improvement in skin tone and texture, with minimal to no active melasma patches

expert_tips: Consult a dermatologist for personalized treatment recommendations and monitoring
Be consistent and patient, as results may take several months of continuous use
Stay hydrated by drinking plenty of water throughout the day
